summary_hint: project name, owner-occupancy %, delinquency %, litigation status, master policy

typed_core.name: project_name
typed_core.why: CO-1 — joins to the appraisal's project_name

typed_core.name: questionnaire_form_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator — Fannie 1076 / Freddie 476 / lender-specific number their questions differently

typed_core.name: completed_date
typed_core.why: CO-1 — a stale questionnaire may not be acceptable

typed_core.name: is_signed
typed_core.why: CO-1 — an unsigned questionnaire is incomplete

typed_core.name: total_units
typed_core.why: CO-5 — the denominator for every percentage

typed_core.name: owner_occupancy_percentage
typed_core.why: CO-5 — stated directly on most forms
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture BOTH the count and the percentage where both are given — a disagreement between them is itself a signal

typed_core.name: single_entity_owned_units
typed_core.why: CO-5 — concentration; a single owner holding too many units breaks warrantability

typed_core.name: commercial_space_percentage
typed_core.why: CO-5 — commercial use above a threshold breaks warrantability

typed_core.name: project_type
typed_core.why: PR-3, CO-5 — established / new / conversion / detached

typed_core.name: is_project_complete
typed_core.why: CO-5 — incomplete phasing is a warrantability issue

typed_core.name: hoa_dues_amount
typed_core.why: DT-2, CO-2 — 'confirm HOA dues are in the payment'

typed_core.name: hoa_dues_frequency
typed_core.why: DT-2 disambiguator — monthly vs annual is a 12x error
typed_core.prompt_hint: ALWAYS state monthly vs annual — never assume

typed_core.name: master_policy_carrier
typed_core.why: CO-3, IH-7 — 'check for the master policy'

typed_core.name: master_policy_coverage_amount
typed_core.why: IH-7 — must equal at least 100% of project replacement cost

typed_core.name: master_policy_replacement_cost_basis
typed_core.why: IH-7, CO-3 — THE IH-1 LESSON APPLIED: a coverage amount alone does not establish adequacy
typed_core.prompt_hint: Look for 'replacement cost', 'guaranteed replacement cost', or 'actual cash value' in the insurance section

typed_core.name: litigation_description
typed_core.why: CO-5 — the NATURE matters: construction-defect litigation is disqualifying, a slip-and-fall usually is not
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the explanation VERBATIM — CO-5 needs the nature, not just the flag

rejected.name: is_warrantable / meets_fannie_guidelines
rejected.reason: A JUDGMENT, NOT A FACT — the whole point of CO-5. Tags describe; rules judge. THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT REJECTION IN THIS SCHEMA

rejected.name: project_facilities (nested list)
rejected.reason: deferred — CO-5's primary signals are all flat percentage fields; a list would cost ~5 plumbing sites for shared-amenity detail no rule reads today

rejected.name: developer_name / year_built
rejected.reason: no consumer today (the appraisal carries year built)

encoding_variations: Fannie 1076 vs Freddie 476 vs lender-specific — the same questions, different numbering
Percentages may be stated directly or require computing from counts
Litigation is often a checkbox plus a free-text explanation
Reserves may be an amount, a percentage of budget, or 'adequate' prose

open_questions.q: Percentages vs counts — compute a missing percentage from counts?
open_questions.recommendation: return as stated — an extractor that computes is doing arithmetic the rule should own
defer — ~5 plumbing sites for detail no rule reads

open_questions.q: The condo master policy is its own document type ('Master Insurance Policy for Condominium')
options: these four fields are a convenience copy
IH-7 reads the master policy document instead
open_questions.recommendation: CONFIRM before relying on them — if IH-7 reads the policy document, the authoritative source is elsewhere and these are a cross-check GEET'S DECISION (LP-435): BOTH — the questionnaire's master-policy fields stay AND the master-policy document is its own source.

notes: NO v2 catalog entry — the rule floor IS the entire schema.

Priya's ruling: condo rules must distinguish WARRANTABLE vs NON-WARRANTABLE projects, not merely check that a questionnaire exists. Warrantability is a CONCLUSION drawn from several facts — this schema captures the facts; CO-5 judges.
All 5 CO rules are BLOCKED on this extractor.
